ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *h₁l̥h₂-tósder. Ancient Greek ἐλᾰστός (elăstós) Proto-Indo-European *-ikos Proto-Italic *-ikos Latin -icus New Latin elasticusbor. French élastiquebor. English elastic From French élastique, from New Latin elasticus (“elastic”), from Ancient Greek ἐλαστός (elastós), alternative form of ἐλατός (elatós, “ductile”) (cf. ἐλατήρ (elatḗr, “a driver, hurler”)), from ἐλαύνω (elaúnō, “to drive, set in motion, push, strike, beat out”).

senses.d: Capable of stretching; particularly, capable of stretching so as to return to an original shape or size when force is released.
ex: The rope is somewhat elastic, so expect it to give when you pull on it.
Demand for entertainment is more elastic than demand for energy.

senses.d: Able to return quickly to a former state or condition, after being depressed or overtaxed; having power to recover easily from shocks and trials.
An elastic material used in clothing, particularly in waistbands and cuffs.
ex: running shorts use elastic to eliminate the need for a belt

ety.text: Borrowed from New Latin elasticus (“elastic”), from Ancient Greek as if *ἐλαστής (*elastḗs) for ἐλατής (elatḗs), equiv. to ἐλατήρ (elatḗr, “a driver, hurler”), from ἐλαύνειν (elaúnein, “to drive, set in motion, push, strike, beat out”). Cognate with Piedmontese elàstich.

From New Latin elasticus (“elastic”), from Ancient Greek as if *ἐλαστής (*elastḗs) for ἐλατής (elatḗs), equivalent to ἐλατήρ (elatḗr, “a driver, hurler”), from ἐλαύνειν (elaúnein, “to drive, set in motion, push, strike, beat out”).
1575, from Late Latin ēlabōrātus (“worked out”), past participle of ēlabōrō (“to work out”), from ē- (“out, forth, fully”) + labor (“work, toil, exertion”). More at e-, labour.

ex: After reading a long, elaborate description, I was impressed but no wiser.
I stared for hours at the elaborate pattern in the rug.

senses.d: Тo develop in detail or complexity.

ex: What do you mean you didn't come home last night? Would you care to elaborate?
Could you elaborate on the plot for your novel for me?

grp.label: to give further detail or explanation
to develop in detail or complexity — see also work out
